evidence.note: CONFIRMED: a baseline-red comparison over failure text truncated to flakes.LINE_CHARS (240) treats two different ratchet causes behind the same visible prefix as the same failure. Regression test test_a_new_cause_hidden_by_a_truncated_failure_text_is_not_baseline_red fails on unfixed code (outcome='partial' baseline-red) and passes after _differs fails-safe on a truncated equality (outcome='failed' new offender).

A bug is not closed without a regression test that fails on the unfixed code (documented in the fix task): added one and watched it fail then pass. A tool that could not run is unavailable, never passed: reviewers/tests are run via their gates. Commit message states the mechanism; no forbidden trailers.
baseline_red._differs now fails safe on a truncated equality: _tally routes the id to 'different' (new offender) so a hidden cause is never read as baseline-red. Regression test covers it.

chunk_findings.detail: An identical, untruncated failure text whose length is exactly `LINE_CHARS` is now classified as a different failure. For example, if `LINE_CHARS == 80` and both the base and branch store `failed_reasons[ID] == "x" * 80` because the real test message is exactly 80 characters long, the previous text is not truncated at all and the cause is the same; the new line still returns `True`, so the gate moves the test into `different`/`new_failures` and reports a regression that does not exist. The method cannot distinguish a truncated-full prefix from an exact whole text, so the “whole text” promise in the docstring is not actually kept; it needs an explicit truncated marker or a digest/full-text comparison.
chunk_findings.location: ddflow/services/gates/baseline_red.py:144 (`return len(base) >= LINE_CHARS or len(branch) >= LINE_CHARS`)
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline_red.py:144 (`return len(base) >= LINE_CHARS or len(branch) >= LINE_CHARS`)

chunk_findings.detail: Given that `branch == base` (both are non-empty strings of length equal to `LINE_CHARS`), the code returns `True` (indicating a different failure/new offender). However, if `branch == base`, it means the truncated failure text on the branch is *identical* to the base, not different. Therefore, when the failure texts are completely identical up to the cut-off point, the code incorrectly flags it as a *different* failure (`True`), whereas identical failure texts should be recognized as the same failure to correctly preserve baseline-red status.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline_red.py:143

chunk_findings.detail: Equal stored reasons are treated as a new cause whenever either string is at least `LINE_CHARS` long, but a cut of `text[:LINE_CHARS]` also yields that length when the full message is exactly `LINE_CHARS` and was not cut. Given base and branch both `"ratchet: found grew past:" + "x" * (LINE_CHARS - len("ratchet: found grew past:"))` (same site, whole text, `len == LINE_CHARS`), the new `return len(base) >= LINE_CHARS or len(branch) >= LINE_CHARS` is True, so the failure is not baseline-red. The same input is what the new test asserts as `different` / `new_failures`, so an unchanged ratchet that merely fills the cap is failed as a branch regression.

chunk_findings.detail: The two signature readers disagree on representation for legacy evidence. A base record produced by the previous flakes.py has only the capped `failed_reasons` text, so `_base_signatures` returns, for test `t`, the display string `"ratchet: found grew past: 30 allowed"`. The branch's new evidence has `failed_reason_hashes`, so `_failure_sigs` returns `content_digest("ratchet: found grew past: 30 allowed")` for the same `t`. `_differs` then computes `branch != base` and reports a new offender for an unchanged failure. This will false-positive against every base record that predates `failed_reason_hashes`, not just truncated/unknown-text cases.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline_red.py:_failure_sigs / _base_signatures

chunk_findings.detail: `failed_reason_hashes` is only populated for `kept` entries with `f["kind"] == "FAILED"`. Reasons added from `errored` (line 164-166 in flakes.py) are present in `failed_reasons` but are never assigned a digest. Because `_failure_sigs` does `ev.get("failed_reason_hashes") or ev.get("failed_reasons")`, one non-empty hash dict makes it discard every `failed_reasons` entry that lacks a hash. Concrete input: base is already red for `test_x` from an old setup error; branch changes that `test_x` to a new setup error while some other test yields `failed_reason_hashes = {"other": digest(...)}`. `_failure_sigs(branch)` omits `test_x`, so `_differs` sees branch missing for `test_x` and returns `False`; the new cause in the already-red `test_x` is hidden. This is the original B-baseline-red-hides-new-cause for non-FAILED reasons.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/flakes.py:139 (_failed_reason_hashes) and ddflow/services/gates/baseline_red.py:141

chunk_findings.detail: The new regression test hand-populates `ev["failed_reason_hashes"]` from the full branch/base reasons and never exercises the changed `ddflow/services/flakes.py` path that is supposed to emit that field. If flakes.py instead records a hash of the truncated display text (`branch_full[:LINE_CHARS]` and `base_full[:LINE_CHARS]`), the branch and base hashes are identical because the prefixes are identical; `GB.apply` then classifies `ID` as baseline-red and the original bug still happens in real CI, while this test still passes because it supplied the differing full-text hashes itself.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_gate_baseline_red.py:test_a_new_cause_hidden_by_a_truncated_failure_text_is_not_baseline_red

chunk_findings.detail: `_failure_sigs` and `_base_signatures` pick `failed_reason_hashes` or `failed_reasons` for the whole map, then `_differs` compares those strings with `!=`. A cached base that only has display text (the "old record" the new docstring allows) against a branch that has digests never matches: given base `failed_reasons[ID] == "x" * LINE_CHARS` and no hashes, and branch `failed_reasons[ID] == "x" * LINE_CHARS` plus `failed_reason_hashes[ID] == content_digest("x" * LINE_CHARS + "same cause")`, the gate treats an unchanged failure as `different` / `new_failures`. The same all-or-nothing choice drops any id that is only in `failed_reasons` once any hash exists, so an ERROR (or any unhashed id) whose text actually changed stays baseline-red.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline_red.py:_failure_sigs

chunk_findings.detail: Parse used to cap every pytest FAILED and ERROR reason at `LINE_CHARS` before it was stored. Truncation was removed there and put back only on the FAILED branch of `_error_fields` (`why[:LINE_CHARS]`), while `errored` is still stored with `reasons.setdefault(tid, why)` and hashes are built only for `kind == "FAILED"`. An ERROR line whose `why` is a multi-megabyte traceback is now written in full into committed `failed_reasons`. That same id is also absent from `failed_reason_hashes`, so once any FAILED hash is present the baseline gate ignores its text entirely.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/flakes.py:79
